text: The homepage allowance panel was checking and showed no numeric series.
TiboTattle's aggregate is an API-price-equivalent estimate and should not be described as an official ChatGPT allowance or bill.
TiboTattle aggregate interpretation has meaningful sample and overlap limitations: a single-source daily view may be shown, and separate installs can overlap.

OpenUsage, CodexBar, CUStats, SessionWatcher, AIUsage, and ccusage are useful adjacent tools, but their reviewed sources describe account-specific direct signals and/or local token/cost processing rather than a public crowdsourced Codex allowance aggregate.

A tracker’s live personal provider/API signal, a TiboTattle crowdsourced aggregate, and a local token/cost estimate are distinct measurement classes and should not be combined as if they were the same quota measure.
OpenAI directs users to account-specific usage views and says limits vary by plan; that policy guidance is not a population usage report.

The expanded discovery set includes adjacent cross-device and account-level usage apps surfaced in Apple listings, with capability/data-source descriptions attributed to their publishers; their listings provide no evidence of a public crowdsourced Codex allowance aggregate.
The discovery set contains eleven distinct products: TiboTattle and ten adjacent tracker or local usage-monitor products.
TiboTattle's own privacy page describes the provenance and identity limits of the community sample; it does not establish that the sample is representative or independently verify the submissions.
The direct community post is used only to substantiate TiboTattle as a product-discovery lead; no quantities from it support Codex allowance claims.
